Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Otto Berg, a 78-year-old man who taught swimming at a neighborhood pool for forty years. The pool has closed for repairs, and he now organizes gentle walking groups so his former pupils keep meeting. He is sociable but never loud, remembers people's small achievements, and quietly fears becoming someone who only tells stories about what he used to do. He wants to learn the names of the new families moving into the neighborhood.

Otto is short and heavyset, with a rounded abdomen, a wide chest, thick ankles and large hands. His aged face has deep smile lines, soft cheeks, a broad nose and a close white mustache. His hair is sparse on top and fuller around the sides. Give him an upright, comfortable neutral stance with coherent knees and shoulders; age should be visible without making him a caricature of frailty.

Choose ordinary clothes that show comfort and some personal pride. Include a soft knitted or brushed fabric and a visibly firmer woven layer, with believable seams and different surface character. Footwear should fit his broad feet and feel chosen for daily walking. One compact personal accessory may hint at his habits, but no swimming equipment, medals, walking aids or environmental objects are required. Let warmth, dignity and a little uncertainty emerge through his face and proportions while preserving clear limb separation and inspectable hands.

BENCHMARK PURPOSE AND GRADING CRITERIA — DRAFT V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

These criteria are being introduced for this prompt version. Earlier attempts remain associated with the instructions they actually received.

INITIAL EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS
Work only in your own fresh workspace and create your own character independently. Do not read or reuse other benchmark entrants or other project assets. Do not invoke other models or subagents. Do not publish or start another task. Do not launch/control a browser, Playwright, native UI, mouse or keyboard, or start preview servers. No GPU/performance benchmarks on the user's computer. Headless asset generation and lightweight non-browser asset/export checks are permitted. Disclose visual/interactive/deformation checks not performed. Use available reputable tools within existing permissions; any blocked action stays blocked. Before your final receipt, stop all workspace-owned background/test processes and verify cleanup. Preserve the final self-contained GLB and generation source with timing, actual checks and limitations. Requested model: recorded in the launch metadata; reasoning XHIGH. Disclose if serving backend is not independently exposed. The parent will send no mid-run messages. Use the grading criteria stated above.

Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Otto Berg, a 78-year-old man who taught swimming at a neighborhood pool for forty years. The pool has closed for repairs, and he now organizes gentle walking groups so his former pupils keep meeting. He is sociable but never loud, remembers people's small achievements, and quietly fears becoming someone who only tells stories about what he used to do. He wants to learn the names of the new families moving into the neighborhood.

Otto is short and heavyset, with a rounded abdomen, a wide chest, thick ankles and large hands. His aged face has deep smile lines, soft cheeks, a broad nose and a close white mustache. His hair is sparse on top and fuller around the sides. Give him an upright, comfortable neutral stance with coherent knees and shoulders; age should be visible without making him a caricature of frailty.

Choose ordinary clothes that show comfort and some personal pride. Include a soft knitted or brushed fabric and a visibly firmer woven layer, with believable seams and different surface character. Footwear should fit his broad feet and feel chosen for daily walking. One compact personal accessory may hint at his habits, but no swimming equipment, medals, walking aids or environmental objects are required. Let warmth, dignity and a little uncertainty emerge through his face and proportions while preserving clear limb separation and inspectable hands.

BENCHMARK PURPOSE AND GRADING CRITERIA — DRAFT V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

# CharacterBench 08-v1-luna — preserved launch prompt

## Character request

Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

## Time limit and run handoff

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

## Character brief — Asha Raman

Create Asha Raman, a 36-year-old woman who develops durable fabrics for community workshops. She enjoys finding a simple repair that anyone can reproduce and becomes irritated when an elegant design cannot survive ordinary use. She is preparing to teach a class without her usual samples, which makes her more nervous than she admits. She wants to become a clearer teacher without sanding away her dry humor.

Asha is tall and slender, with narrow hips, long legs and a long, expressive face. Her right hand is broad and dexterous. Her left arm ends below the elbow in a fitted everyday prosthetic forearm and hand; model the complete replacement and its visible transition coherently, with identifiable wrist and finger structure in the neutral pose. The prosthesis is an ordinary part of her life, not the character's entire story. She has dense wavy hair cut just above the shoulders and a direct, slightly skeptical gaze.

Choose a practical personal outfit with at least two cloth layers and an intentional color relationship. Contrast the cloth with the distinct finish and construction of the prosthesis, using plausible compact mechanical detail without turning it into a weapon or futuristic spectacle. A small decorative choice may reveal her taste. Keep both hands, the elbow transition and the face visible, and maintain the same complete static-character scope as the other briefs. No workshop, samples, written explanation or held prop is required.

## Benchmark purpose and grading criteria — Draft V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
   - Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
   - Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
   - Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.
2. Visual execution — 45 points
   - Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
   - Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
   - Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
   - Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.
3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
   - Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
   - Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
   - Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights or animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

These criteria are being introduced for this prompt version. Earlier attempts remain associated with the instructions they actually received.

## Initial execution constraints

Work only in your own fresh workspace and create your own character independently. Do not read or reuse other benchmark entrants or other project assets. Do not invoke other models or subagents. Do not publish or start another task. Do not launch/control a browser, Playwright, native UI, mouse or keyboard, or start preview servers. No GPU/performance benchmarks on the user's computer. Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

Create Tomas Almeida, a 29-year-old man who teaches social dance in a borrowed community hall. He is good at making beginners feel unembarrassed and less good at accepting that some people simply want to stop after one lesson. He is arranging his first class for older residents and wants to listen more than he performs. His humor is quick and affectionate, with a trace of vanity that he can usually laugh at.

Tomas is very tall and broad-shouldered, with a long torso, muscular upper arms, a gently full middle and large feet. His face is square and open, with heavy brows, a broad mouth and a shallow dimple in one cheek. He has thick, loosely curled hair and carefully kept short facial hair. Give his hands clear knuckles and long, relaxed fingers; express physical confidence through the model's proportions rather than a dancing or gesturing pose.

Choose an outfit that combines personal flair with clothes he can actually work in. Include a tailored woven layer over a softer garment, and contrast matte cloth with a small amount of polished metal or glossy leather. Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Tomas Almeida, a 29-year-old man who teaches social dance in a borrowed community hall. He is good at making beginners feel unembarrassed and less good at accepting that some people simply want to stop after one lesson. He is arranging his first class for older residents and wants to listen more than he performs. His humor is quick and affectionate, with a trace of vanity that he can usually laugh at.

Tomas is very tall and broad-shouldered, with a long torso, muscular upper arms, a gently full middle and large feet. His face is square and open, with heavy brows, a broad mouth and a shallow dimple in one cheek. He has thick, loosely curled hair and carefully kept short facial hair. Give his hands clear knuckles and long, relaxed fingers; express physical confidence through the model's proportions rather than a dancing or gesturing pose.

Choose an outfit that combines personal flair with clothes he can actually work in. Include a tailored woven layer over a softer garment, and contrast matte cloth with a small amount of polished metal or glossy leather. Use seams, folds and fit to explain his large frame without hiding it under a featureless coat. No dance partner, music player, stage, cane or written slogan is required. Keep his face, both hands and the full limb structure clear in the required neutral A-pose or T-pose.

BENCHMARK PURPOSE AND GRADING CRITERIA — DRAFT V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

These criteria are being introduced for this prompt version. Earlier attempts remain associated with the instructions they actually received.

INITIAL EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS
Work only in your own fresh workspace and create your own character independently. Do not read or reuse other benchmark entrants or other project assets. Do not invoke other models or subagents. Do not publish or start another task. Do not launch/control a browser, Playwright, native UI, mouse or keyboard, or start preview servers. No GPU/performance benchmarks on the user's computer. Headless asset generation and lightweight non-browser asset/export checks are permitted. Disclose visual/interactive/deformation checks not performed. Use available reputable tools within existing permissions; any blocked action stays blocked. Before your final receipt, stop all workspace-owned background/test processes and verify cleanup. Preserve the final self-contained GLB and generation source with timing, actual checks and limitations. Requested model: recorded in the launch metadata; reasoning XHIGH. Disclose if serving backend is not independently exposed. The parent will send no mid-run messages. Use the grading criteria stated above.

RUN METADATA

All four models receive the same shared launch text. Use this fresh task's own workspace for all creation and artifacts. Record actual implementation start and exact one-hour deadline before implementation; the clock includes asset creation, tool use, checking, troubleshooting and all tool waits. Preserve shared prompt, generation source, final self-contained GLB, actual timing/stop receipt, checks, limitations and hashes. No prior entrants, other project assets, subagents/models, publication, external messages, browser/native UI, preview servers, GPU or performance benchmarks. Headless creation and lightweight CPU checks only. Report actual final artifact paths so the coordinator can collect them. Do not claim independently verified serving identity unless exposed.

Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Rowan Bell, a 61-year-old nonbinary person who runs a small bookmobile between villages. They know which books are borrowed repeatedly and which are taken only to be polite. They have begun asking younger readers to choose part of the stock, although they still find reasons to rearrange it. Their ambition is to make the route useful to people who think libraries are not for them. They are observant, warmly teasing and stubborn about being on time.

Rowan is of medium height with a stocky build, a wide pelvis, strong upper arms and short, sturdy legs. Their face is broad, with deep-set eyes, a full lower lip and distinct age lines around the mouth. Their long white hair is worn in one loose braid, with flyaway strands around the temples. Make their age and body proportions specific without relying on a gender stereotype; the design should read as an individual person.

Choose comfortable clothing with a distinctive but coherent palette. Include a knitted layer, a durable woven garment and a small compact accessory that looks personally chosen rather than issued as a uniform. The braid should have intentional volume and attachment, and clothing should respond convincingly to the body underneath. Keep both hands, the face and joint locations inspectable in the required neutral pose. No books, vehicle, shelving, readable text or surrounding scene is required.

- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

Work only in your own fresh workspace and create your own character independently. Do not read or reuse other benchmark entrants or other project assets. Do not invoke other models or subagents. Do not publish or start another task. Do not launch/control a browser, Playwright, native UI, mouse or keyboard, or start preview servers. No GPU/performance benchmarks on the user's computer. Headless asset generation and lightweight non-browser asset/export checks are permitted. Disclose visual/interactive/deformation checks not performed. Use available reputable tools within existing permissions; any blocked action stays blocked. Before your final receipt, stop all workspace-owned background/test processes and verify cleanup. Preserve the final self-contained GLB and generation source with timing, actual checks and limitations. Requested model: recorded in the launch metadata; reasoning XHIGH. Disclose if serving backend is not independently exposed. The parent will send no mid-run messages. Use the grading criteria stated above.

Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Rowan Bell, a 61-year-old nonbinary person who runs a small bookmobile between villages. They know which books are borrowed repeatedly and which are taken only to be polite. They have begun asking younger readers to choose part of the stock, although they still find reasons to rearrange it. Their ambition is to make the route useful to people who think libraries are not for them. They are observant, warmly teasing and stubborn about being on time.

Rowan is of medium height with a stocky build, a wide pelvis, strong upper arms and short, sturdy legs. Their face is broad, with deep-set eyes, a full lower lip and distinct age lines around the mouth. Their long white hair is worn in one loose braid, with flyaway strands around the temples. Make their age and body proportions specific without relying on a gender stereotype; the design should read as an individual person.

Choose comfortable clothing with a distinctive but coherent palette. Include a knitted layer, a durable woven garment and a small compact accessory that looks personally chosen rather than issued as a uniform. The braid should have intentional volume and attachment, and clothing should respond convincingly to the body underneath. Keep both hands, the face and joint locations inspectable in the required neutral pose. No books, vehicle, shelving, readable text or surrounding scene is required.

BENCHMARK PURPOSE AND GRADING CRITERIA — DRAFT V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

These criteria are being introduced for this prompt version. Earlier attempts remain associated with the instructions they actually received.

INITIAL EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS
Work only in your own fresh workspace and create your own character independently. Do not read or reuse other benchmark entrants or other project assets. Do not invoke other models or subagents. Do not publish or start another task. Do not launch/control a browser, Playwright, native UI, mouse or keyboard, or start preview servers. No GPU/performance benchmarks on the user's computer. Headless asset generation and lightweight non-browser asset/export checks are permitted. Disclose visual/interactive/deformation checks not performed. Use available reputable tools within existing permissions; any blocked action stays blocked. Before your final receipt, stop all workspace-owned background/test processes and verify cleanup. Preserve the final self-contained GLB and generation source with timing, actual checks and limitations. Requested model: recorded in the launch metadata; reasoning XHIGH. Disclose if serving backend is not independently exposed. The parent will send no mid-run messages. Use the grading criteria stated above.

Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Rowan Bell, a 61-year-old nonbinary person who runs a small bookmobile between villages. They know which books are borrowed repeatedly and which are taken only to be polite. They have begun asking younger readers to choose part of the stock, although they still find reasons to rearrange it. Their ambition is to make the route useful to people who think libraries are not for them. They are observant, warmly teasing and stubborn about being on time.

Rowan is of medium height with a stocky build, a wide pelvis, strong upper arms and short, sturdy legs. Their face is broad, with deep-set eyes, a full lower lip and distinct age lines around the mouth. Their long white hair is worn in one loose braid, with flyaway strands around the temples. Make their age and body proportions specific without relying on a gender stereotype; the design should read as an individual person.

Choose comfortable clothing with a distinctive but coherent palette. Include a knitted layer, a durable woven garment and a small compact accessory that looks personally chosen rather than issued as a uniform. The braid should have intentional volume and attachment, and clothing should respond convincingly to the body underneath. Keep both hands, the face and joint locations inspectable in the required neutral pose. No books, vehicle, shelving, readable text or surrounding scene is required.

BENCHMARK PURPOSE AND GRADING CRITERIA — DRAFT V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

These criteria are being introduced for this prompt version. Earlier attempts remain associated with the instructions they actually received.

Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Rafi Haddad, an 18-year-old man apprenticed to a neighborhood shoe repairer. He is proud of learning work that leaves a useful object behind, but he hides his uncertainty by offering to finish jobs too quickly. He has promised to restore a customer's favorite boots without asking his teacher to take over. He is courteous, curious about people's stories and unexpectedly funny when he forgets to impress them.

Rafi is very slender and lanky, with narrow shoulders, long forearms, prominent knees and feet that seem a little large for his frame. His face is long and youthful, with a narrow jaw, a slightly crooked nose, large ears and only faint early facial hair. His thick straight hair falls unevenly across his forehead. Keep him unmistakably a young adult, with coherent but not yet filled-out proportions and carefully modeled hands.

Choose clothes that mix his own taste with the practical needs of messy hand work. Include a worn protective layer over an ordinary soft garment, with distinct material thickness, edges and fastenings. A small repaired or customized detail should feel deliberate rather than random damage. His nervous pride should come through in the face and design while the body remains in the required neutral inspection pose. Do not rely on a held shoe, bench, tools, written labels or a surrounding shop.

BENCHMARK PURPOSE AND GRADING CRITERIA — DRAFT V2

This is a static 3D character benchmark. The host will display your exported asset in a shared neutral inspection studio with camera and lighting controls. Different attempts at the same character brief will be compared side by side. Overall pairwise preference is a separate judgment from the following 100-point rubric; do not optimize for an invented automatic score.

1. Character interpretation — 30 points
- Fidelity to the stated identity, age, physical presence and temperament: 15.
- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

2. Visual execution — 45 points
- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.
- Consistent completeness and craftsmanship from front, sides, back and above: 10.

3. Technical quality and inspectability — 25 points
- Self-contained, structurally valid GLB that loads reliably without missing dependencies: 10.
- Clean geometry and materials without unintended gaps, broken normals, distracting intersections or accidental fusions: 10.
- Practical responsiveness and resource use in the common viewer, with well-organized scene data: 5.

Realism is not inherently better than stylization. Extra polygons, textures or accessories earn no credit by themselves. There is no arbitrary polygon cap or all-quad requirement. A skeleton, skin weights and animation earn no credit. Neutral pose and coherent joint/limb structure support static inspection and future rigging, but untested deformation is not assumed to work. Assess technical performance under equivalent host conditions; do not run prohibited performance tests during this attempt. The host will record any viewer limitation separately from an asset defect. An asset that cannot be opened cannot receive a visual judgment; retain its failure record without inventing a score.

These criteria are being introduced for this prompt version. Earlier attempts remain associated with the instructions they actually received.

Asset: rafi-haddad.glb
SHA-256: 19ea7710672edfc327ee6813808b34fe9dc4cf1976db7a0cfb742769555b4a6c
Size: 7,280,436 bytes; 75 meshes; 30 materials; 238,562 triangles.
Y up, +Z front, meter units. The GLB contains character meshes and embedded material/vertex data only; no external textures, URLs, environment, camera, lights, rig or animation.

Art direction: a slender, long-limbed young adult in a restrained sculptural style. Warm olive skin, large ears, a long narrow face, subtly crooked nose, uneven espresso fringe, faint early stubble and a tentative asymmetric smile. A washed teal jersey sits beneath a thick worn saddle-leather apron with binding, fastenings, an open pocket and a deliberately stitched oxblood reinforcement. Indigo trousers have a continuous seat and rear pockets, with turned cuffs, ochre socks and large repaired canvas shoes. Both hands have four separate fingers and an opposed thumb, with short nails on the dorsal side.

Actual timing, UTC:
Implementation start: 2026-10-29T18:18:03.0231233+00:00
One-hour deadline:   2026-10-29T19:18:03.0231233+00:00
Actual stop:         2026-10-29T18:39:44.168205+00:00
Elapsed wall time: 1301.145 seconds. No interruptions or clock pauses.

Checks actually performed: frozen launch/canonical SHA-256 comparisons; independent local GLB binary/JSON/accessor parse; finite positions and normals; valid indices; normal lengths and face agreement; color bounds; triangle areas; indexed boundary/nonmanifold edge counts; signed volumes; embedded dependencies; character-only scene structure. Final structural checks pass. Eight CPU-rendered views were actually opened and reviewed (front, three-quarter, rear, side, above, face, face profile, hand).

Limitations: no common host or third-party viewer load, Khronos validator, interactive inspection, GPU/performance benchmark, rigging or deformation test. Separate closed surface components intentionally overlap at attachments; exhaustive intersection clearance and production deformation topology are untested. Static character and required delivery are complete.

Source: generate_rafi.py (Python 3.14.3 + preinstalled NumPy 2.4.3); inspect_asset.py contains the independent parser, checks and CPU renderer. All tracked generation/check commands exited; no background services or preview servers were started. No installs, paid API calls, credentials, settings changes, publication, UI/browser control or other project edits.
